ABOUT THIS EDITION

The Arabic Easy-to-Read Version (al-Kitab al-Muqaddas: at-Tarjama al-Arabiyya al-Mubassata) is a complete Bible in Standard Arabic published by Bible League International (originally the World Bible Translation Center, Fort Worth, Texas). The current edition is copyright 2016. It is a thought-for-thought translation designed for accessibility and clarity, part of the ERV (Easy-to-Read Version) family. An earlier edition was published around 2009.

ABOUT THIS EDITION

The New Arabic Version (NAV), known in Arabic as Kitab al-Hayat (كتاب الحياة, "Book of Life"), is a modern Arabic Bible translation initiated in 1973 by Living Bibles International under the direction of Georges Houssney, a Lebanese Christian based in Beirut. Houssney employed two key translators: Said Baz, who completed the New Testament in 1982, and Dr. Samuel Shahid, who completed the Old Testament in 1988. The translation philosophy was modeled after the New International Version (NIV), and it was originally titled "Book of Life, an interpretive translation" (كتاب الحياة ترجمة تفسيرية). When Living Bibles International merged with the International Bible Society in 1992, the translation was renamed the New Arabic Version (NAV). The NAV has achieved wide acceptance throughout the Arab world, with several million copies in circulation, making it one of the most popular contemporary Arabic Bible translations. It was revised in 1997 and again in 2012 and is released under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 license as the "Open New Arabic Version."

ABOUT THIS EDITION

The most popular Arabic translation is the Van Dyck Version, funded by the Syrian Mission and the American Bible Society. The project was the brainchild of Eli Smith, and started around 1847, centered in Beirut. After Eli Smith's death it was completed under the direction of Cornelius Van Alen Van Dyck. Others involved included Nasif al Yaziji, Boutros al Bustani, and Yusuf al-Asir. The New Testament was completed on March 9, 1860, followed by the Old Testament on March 10, 1865. It remains widely used across Arab churches.

ABOUT THIS EDITION

The Egyptian Arabic Translation (EAT) is a complete Bible in colloquial Egyptian Arabic (Masri), produced by Wycliffe Bible Translators and published by the United Bible Societies. Egyptian Arabic is the most widely spoken Arabic vernacular, with approximately 68 million native speakers, and is linguistically distinct from Modern Standard Arabic (MSA) used in most other Arabic Bible translations. The EAT aims to make the Scriptures accessible in the everyday spoken language of Egypt, using vocabulary common to the colloquial register rather than the formal literary Arabic of classical translations. This is significant because many Egyptians, particularly those with limited formal education, find MSA texts difficult to understand. The translation copyright is held by Wycliffe Bible Translators, Inc.

ABOUT THIS EDITION

The Hadrami Arabic Translation (2010) is a Scripture portion translation into Hadrami Arabic (ISO 639-3: ayh), a spoken Arabic variety of the Hadhramaut region in southeastern Yemen. An estimated 4.9–6 million people speak Hadrami Arabic, primarily in the Hadhramaut and adjacent governorates of Yemen, with diaspora communities across the Horn of Africa, East Africa, and Southeast Asia. The translation was produced by Wycliffe Bible Translators, Inc. (copyright 1999–2016) and comprises a limited selection of biblical texts at 52 printed pages.

ABOUT THIS EDITION

This edition is identified in its metadata as the Syriac Bible (Peshitto), a New Testament published by the Bible Society of Turkey in 2012. The Peshitta (also spelled Peshitto) is the standard Syriac version of the Bible, with the Old Testament translated largely from Hebrew (with some influence from the Septuagint and Targums) by the 2nd century CE, and the New Testament translated from Koine Greek probably in the early 5th century. The name "Peshitta" derives from the Syriac for "simple" or "common," first attested in the 9th century. The Peshitta has been the authoritative Bible of Syriac-speaking Christian communities since the 5th century and has influenced the Armenian, Georgian, Arabic, and Persian versions.

Note on language classification: The metadata for this edition assigns the ISO 639-3 code ayp (North Mesopotamian Arabic), but the Peshitta is written in Classical Syriac, a literary dialect of Aramaic (ISO 639-3: syc). This appears to be a cataloging error; the text is Syriac/Aramaic, not Arabic.

1. البداية

التكوين 1:1

1. البداية

التكوين 1:1

تنسجم قصة يسوع مع القصة الأكبر للتقاليد اليهودية المسيحية. كان الغرض من كل شيء منذ الخلق هو الإشارة إلى حياة يسوع.\ \ كل الخليقة تتحدث عن عظمة الله. عندما خلق الله الرجل والمرأة، كان يقصد أن يعيشوا في سلام معه إلى الأبد. ولكن بسبب عصيانهم، انفصل البشر عن الله. لكن الله ما زال يحب البشرية، لذلك يكشف الله في جميع أنحاء الكتاب المقدس عن خطته لإنقاذ العالم.

بعد أسبوع من ولادة الطفل، تم ختانه وأطلق عليه رسميًا اسم يسوع. عندما كان يسوع صبيًا صغيرًا، ذهبوا إلى الهيكل حيث التقوا برجل اسمه سمعان.\ \ كان الروح القدس قد أكد لسمعان أنه لن يموت قبل أن يرى مسيح الرب. رأى سمعان يسوع وأعلن أنه المسيح الموعود.

لوقا 3:1

يوحنا المعمدان ينادي في الصحراء. ويبشر على ضفاف نهر الأردن قائلاً: \"توبوا عن خطاياكم وتعمّدوا، فيغفر لكم الله خطاياكم.\" إنه الشخص الذي تنبأ إشعياء بأنه سيمهد الطريق للرب. تتجمع الحشود. وعلى الفور، يحذرهم ألا يكتفوا بالقول إنهم تابوا. بل عليهم أن يتبعوا التوبة بأفعال تظهر تغييراً في قلوبهم. يركع عند أقدام شخص أقل منه ليتعمّد. يظهر لنا كيف يجب أن نكون متواضعين.

5. الشيطان يغوي يسوع

بعد أن تعمد يسوع، قاده الروح إلى الصحراء. يقضي هناك 40 يوماً، يتعرض خلالها لإغراءات الشيطان المستمرة. طوال تلك الفترة، لم يأكل شيئًا. \ \ يحاول الشيطان إغواء يسوع، لكن يسوع يجيب باستخدام الكتاب المقدس، ويقاومه.

6. يسوع يعلن تحقيق نبوءات الكتاب المقدس

لوقا 4:14

عندما يعود يسوع إلى الناصرة، يذهب إلى الكنيس. يُطلب منه قراءة الكتاب المقدس ويُعطى كتاب إشعياء. ومنه يقرأ إشعياء 61: 1-2. \ \ تتحدث النبوءة عن إحضار البشارة للفقراء، وإعلان الحرية للأسرى، واستعادة البصر للمكفوفين، وتحرير المظلومين، وإعلان أن الوقت قد حان لكي يخلص الرب شعبه. \ \ عندما ينتهي من القراءة، يعلن يسوع للناس أن النبوءة قد تحققت كما قرأها للتو.

7. مثل الفريسي والعشار

7. مثل الفريسي والعشار

لوقا 18:9

يعلم يسوع من قارب قبالة شاطئ بحيرة جينيساريت. يتكلم بأمثال، ويضرب مثالاً بفريسي وجابي ضرائب يذهبان إلى الهيكل للصلاة. يختلف الرجلان في طريقة تعاملهما مع الصلاة. يشكر الله لأنه ليس جشعًا أو كاذبًا أو زانيًا مثل الآخرين. يشير بشكل خاص إلى جابي الضرائب ويشكر الله لأنه ليس مثله. يخبر الفريسي الله بجرأة بما يفعله: يصوم يومين في الأسبوع ويقدم عُشر دخله.\ \ يقف جابي الضرائب على مسافة من المذبح. يضرب على صدره ورأسه منحني. الشيء الوحيد الذي يصلي به هو: \"يا الله، ارحمني أنا الخاطئ!

8. الصيد المعجزي للأسماك

لوقا 5:1

8. الصيد المعجزي للأسماك

لوقا 5:1

يطلب يسوع من الصياد صاحب القارب أن يبحر أبعد ويطرح شباكه. يتذمر الصياد قائلاً إنه هو والآخرون قد قضوا الليل كله في البحر. ولم يصطادوا شيئاً.\ يوافق الصياد على الخروج ويستدعي شركاءه. يجلس يسوع في القارب مع الصياد. ينتظر بفارغ الصبر. ثم يجمع الشباك، ويخرج شيئًا ما ببطء إلى السطح.\ \ يضحك بفرح عندما يرى الشباك مليئة بالأسماك التي ترفرف. \ \ عندما ينتهون، يجلس الصياد في قارب مليء بالأسماك. ينظر إلى يسوع. يعبس الصياد ويقول: \"ابتعد عني يا رب. أنا رجل خاطئ.\" يقول له يسوع ألا يخاف، وأنه من الآن فصاعدًا سيكون صيادًا للبشر.

9. إحياء ابنة يائيروس

لوقا 8:41

9. إحياء ابنة يائيروس

لوقا 8:41

تزاحم الحشود على يسوع وهو يغادر الكنيس. صوت واحد يعلو على الأصوات الأخرى. رجل، يائيروس، يتوسل إلى يسوع أن يخلص ابنته المريضة البالغة من العمر 12 عامًا. \ \ يركض رجل آخر إلى يائيروس. ويخبره ألا يزعج المعلم، لأن ابنته قد ماتت. يستدير يسوع ويخبره ألا يخاف. وأنه إذا آمن يائيروس، فستكون ابنته بخير.\ \ يزور يسوع والتلاميذ العائلة. الجيران يبكون على فقدان الابنة. وهي ترقد بلا حياة على سرير. ينظر يسوع إليها للحظة. ثم ينظر إلى والدة الطفلة ويواسيها. يقول إن الطفلة لم تمت، بل إنها في الحقيقة نائمة فقط. \ \ يجلس يسوع وينظر إلى الفتاة للحظة، ثم يقول لها أن تنهض.

10. اختيار التلاميذ

لوقا 5:27

10. اختيار التلاميذ

لوقا 5:27

يرى يسوع جابي ضرائب يدعى متى لوي عند البوابة. يجمع متى رسوم الجمارك من المارة. عندما ينظر إليه يسوع، يشعر متى بذلك ويرفع رأسه. يقول له يسوع: \"اتبعني\".\ \ ينظر متى إليه وهو يذهب للحظة. بصمت، يقف ويترك كل شيء ليتبع يسوع. في وقت لاحق، يصعد يسوع إلى التل ليصلي. يصلي طوال الليل إلى الله. عندما ينزل من التل في صباح اليوم التالي، يجمع أتباعه. ومن بينهم، يختار 12 رسولاً. \ \ كان سمعان (الذي سماه يسوع بطرس) وشقيقه أندراوس صيادين شهدا معجزة صيد السمك الوفير. ثم يختار يسوع يعقوب ويوحنا، وفيلبس وبرثولماوس. ويختار متى، جابي الضرائب الذي دعاه عند البوابة. وأخيرًا يختار يسوع توما، يعقوب بن حلفاي، سمعان الغيور، يهوذا بن يعقوب، ويهوذا الإسخريوطي، الذي سيخون يسوع.

ينظر يسوع إلى الحشود التي تجمعت لسماعه يتكلم. ولكن بدلاً من التحدث إلى الجماهير، التفت يسوع إلى تلاميذه. وشجعهم على مواصلة رحلتهم. \ \ وأكد لهم أنهم مباركون عندما يكرههم الناس ويرفضونهم ويهينونهم ويقولون إنهم أشرار لأنهم يتبعون يسوع. وشجعهم على أن يكونوا سعداء ويرقصوا فرحًا عندما يحدث ذلك. لأنهم سيحصلون على مكافأة عظيمة في السماء. ويذكرهم بأن أسلافهم تصرفوا بنفس الطريقة تجاه الأنبياء.

دعا فريسي يسوع لتناول العشاء في منزله. كانوا يتناولون الطعام عندما اقتربت امرأة من يسوع. نظر إليها الجميع في المنزل، بما في ذلك الفريسي. \ \ روى يسوع للفريسي قصة. قال إن هناك رجلين مدينين لشخص ما. أحدهما مدين بـ 500 قطعة فضية. والآخر مدين بـ 50 قطعة. لم يستطع أي منهما سداد دينه. لذلك ألغى المقرض كلا الدينين. يسأل يسوع أي الرجلين أحب المقرض أكثر لما فعله.

1. The Beginning

Genesis 1:1

1. The Beginning

Genesis 1:1

The story of Jesus fits within the larger story of the Judeo Christian tradition. The purpose of everything since creation has been to point to the life of Jesus. All of creation speaks of the majesty of God. As God created man and woman he intended them to live in peace with him forever. But because of their disobedience mankind was separated from God. But God still loved mankind so throughout the Scriptures God reveals his plan to save the world.

3:43
2. Birth Of Jesus

Luke 1:1

2. Birth Of Jesus

Luke 1:1

Luke makes his introduction as the careful author of this Gospel. The angel Gabriel appears to Mary, a virgin in Nazareth. He announces to her that she has found favor with God and will give birth to Jesus, the Son of God. Through Jesus' birth, prophecies are fulfilled by the arrangement of events. God leaves no detail unnoticed. The same can be said of our own lives.

2:15
3. Childhood Of Jesus

Luke 2:21

3. Childhood Of Jesus

Luke 2:21

One week after the baby is born, He is circumcised and officially named Jesus. While Jesus is a small boy they go to the temple where they meet a man named Simeon. The Holy Spirit had assured Simeon he would not die before seeing the Lord's Messiah. Simeon sees Jesus and declares Him the promised Messiah.

4. Baptism Of Jesus By John

Luke 3:1

4. Baptism Of Jesus By John

Luke 3:1

John the Baptist calls out in the desert. He preaches by the river Jordan, "Turn away from your sins and be baptized, and God will forgive your sins." He is the one Isaiah predicted would make way for the Lord. The crowds gather. Immediately, he warns them not to only say they have repented. Instead, they're to follow repentance with actions that exhibit a changed heart. Jesus is baptized and receives the Holy Spirit. He kneels at the feet of someone lesser than Himself to be baptized. He demonstrates how we are to be humble.

2:22
5. The Devil Tempts Jesus

Luke 4:1

5. The Devil Tempts Jesus

Luke 4:1

After Jesus has been baptized, He's led by the Spirit into the desert. He spends 40 days there, constantly tempted by the devil. All that time, he eats nothing. The devil tries to tempt Jesus, but Jesus answers using Scripture, resisting him.

3:07
6. Jesus Proclaims Fulfillment Of The Scriptures

Luke 4:14

6. Jesus Proclaims Fulfillment Of The Scriptures

Luke 4:14

When Jesus returns to Nazareth, He goes to the synagogue. He's asked to read the Scriptures and is handed the Book of Isaiah. From it, He reads Isaiah 61:1-2. The prophecy speaks of bringing good news to the poor, proclaiming liberty to the captives, recovery of sight to the blind, freeing the oppressed, and announcing that it's time the Lord will save His people. When He finishes reading, Jesus announces to the people that the prophecy has come true as it was just read.

1:02
7. Parable Of The Pharisee And Tax Collector

Luke 18:9

7. Parable Of The Pharisee And Tax Collector

Luke 18:9

Jesus teaches from a boat off the shore of Lake Gennesaret. He speaks in parables, giving the example of a Pharisee and tax collector going to the temple to pray. The two men approach prayer very differently. The Pharisee in the story stands by himself and lists his respectable attributes. He thanks God that he is not greedy, dishonest, or an adulterer like everyone else. He specifically points out the tax collector and thanks God for not being like him. The Pharisee boldly tells God what he does: He fasts two days a week and gives a tenth of his income. The tax collector stands at a distance from the altar. Head bowed, he beats on his chest. The only thing he prays is, "God, have pity on me, a sinner!"

8. Miraculous Catch Of Fish

Luke 5:1

8. Miraculous Catch Of Fish

Luke 5:1

Jesus tells the fisherman who owns it to push out farther and let down their nets. The fisherman grumbles that he and the others have already been out all night long. They didn't catch anything. The fisherman agrees to go out and calls to his partners. Jesus sits in the boat with the fisherman. He waits expectantly. Then gathers the nets, slowly bringing something to the surface. He laughs with joy when he sees the nets are full of flopping fish. When they're done, the fisherman sits in a boat full of fish. He looks up to Jesus. The fisherman frowns and says, "Go away from me, Lord. I am a sinful man." Jesus tells him not to be afraid, that from then on, he would be a fisher of men.

Crowds press in on Jesus as He leaves the synagogue. One voice rises above the others. A man, Jairus, begs Jesus to save his sick, 12-year-old daughter. Another man runs up to Jairus. He tells him not to bother the teacher, that his daughter has died. Jesus turns and tells him not to be afraid. And that if Jairus would believe, his daughter would be well. Jesus and the disciples visit the family. The neighbors wail for the loss of the daughter. She lies lifeless on a cot. Jesus looks at her for a moment. Then He looks to the child’s mother and comforts her. He says the child isn't dead, but that she’s actually just asleep. Jesus sits and looks at the girl for a moment, then tells her to rise.

Luke 5:27

Jesus spots a tax collector named Matthew Levi at the gate. He collects toll money for customs as people pass through. As Jesus looks at him, Matthew senses it and looks up. Jesus says, "Follow me." Matthew watches Him go for a moment. Silently, he stands and leaves everything to follow Jesus. Later Jesus goes up a hill to pray. He prays the entire night to God. When He comes down from the hill the next morning, He gathers His followers. From them, he chooses 12 apostles. Simon (who Jesus named Peter) and Simon's brother Andrew had been the fishermen who experienced the miracle of a large catch of fish. Then Jesus chooses James and John, Philip and Bartholomew. And He chooses Matthew, the tax collector he had called at the gate. And finally Jesus chooses Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who would betray Jesus.

11. Beatitudes

Jesus looks out over the crowds gathered to hear him speak. But instead of speaking to the masses, Jesus turns back to his disciples. He encourages them for the journey ahead. He assures them that they are blessed when people hate them, reject them, insult them, and say that they are evil because they follow Jesus. He encourages them to be happy and dance for joy when that happens. Because there will be great reward in heaven for them. And He reminds them that their ancestors acted the same way toward prophets.

12. Sermon On The Mount

Jesus turns to the crowds and walks through them, teaching. He advises everyone how to walk through life in love. And talks of how, out of pride, we often judge others. He implores those who are listening to love their enemies, to actively pray for them. He speaks of offering more than what is asked of you. Do for others what you would have them do for you.

13. Blessed Are Those Who Hear And Obey

Jesus reminds us that those who hear and obey are blessed.

14. Sinful Woman Forgiven

A Pharisee invites Jesus to have dinner at His house. They're eating when a woman approaches Jesus. Everyone in the house stares, including the Pharisee. Jesus tells the Pharisee a story. He says that there were two men who owed money to someone. One owed 500 silver coins. The other owed 50. Neither men could pay their debt. So the lender canceled both debts. Jesus asks which man loved the lender more for what he'd done.

15. Women Disciples

Jesus continues through the countryside. He's adamant in preaching the good news about the kingdom of God. The twelve disciples follow him. And some women follow as well. They serve the disciples, using their own resources to aid the ministry of Jesus.

Herod has thrown John the Baptist into prison. Messengers come to him in the prison. They relay to him all that Jesus has been doing. Specifically, they tell him about a funeral procession where Jesus sees the widow who has lost her son. His heart fills with compassion. He tells the young man to get up! The son rises from the dead and goes back with his mother. After hearing this, John asks them to go ask Jesus if He's the Messiah, or if they should expect someone else. The messengers arrive where Jesus is sleeping and ask Him what John wants to know.

17. Parable Of The Sower And The Seed

The crowds press in on Jesus as He walks and teaches. He tells a parable of someone sowing seeds of grain in a field. The seed falls in a number of places, each representing something to the crowd. A disciple asks Jesus why He speaks in parables. Jesus explains the parable to the disciples. The seed that's scattered is the Word of God.

18. Parable Of The Lamp

Jesus uses a torch to explain how his followers should live. No one covers the light or puts it under a bed. Instead, they put it in a place where people will see the light when they come in. Jesus gets into a boat and tells His disciples they should all go to the other side of the lake. Along the way, Jesus falls asleep. A storm starts to rage. Waves stretch high over the bow. And the boat starts to take on water. The whole time, Jesus stays asleep. The disciples hold on tight. They try to keep the boat afloat. Finally, Peter cries out to the still sleeping Jesus. He tells Jesus that the boat is taking on water and that they'll all be drowned. Jesus stands and puts a hand out toward the storm. The storm clears. And the seas immediately calm.

At first the man won't say. But Jesus holds out a hand to him. He says his name is Legion. He begs not to be sent back to the abyss. Instead, he wants to go into a nearby herd of pigs. Jesus puts a hand out to the pigs.

Jesus considers this and tells the disciples to feed the people. Mary Magdalene points out that they only have a few loaves of bread and two fish. Jesus takes the baskets and proclaims to the heavens and the people, "Blessed is the Lord God, King of the Universe who brings forth bread from the earth."

Jesus stares back at him.

He starts talking to two men who seem to be with Him. Moses and Elijah speak to Him. One says Jesus will fulfill God's purpose. The other says He will die in Jerusalem. Peter slowly wakes up. Jesus gently tells the man to bring his son closer. Two men carry the boy to Jesus. But he falls again into another fit. Jesus comes to stand over him. The boy looks up. And slowly, he gets up. Now, where there were cuts and bruises on his face, there are none.

The Covenant in Arabic — Lumo Project Films' word-for-word film of the Torah, told through the eyes of Ezra, with Arabic narration over cinematic footage. Presented as 12 chapters plus the full film. Arabic is spoken mainly in Saudi Arabia by around 350,000,000 people.

Chapter 1

عزرا يدخل أورشليم

Chapter 1

Frame narrative — Ezra in Jerusalem

عزرا يدخل أورشليم

الإطار السردي الافتتاحي. يعود الكاهن الكاتب عزرا إلى أورشليم ويستعد لرواية قصة عهد الله مع إسرائيل — مهيِّئًا المشهد لإعادة سرد عظيمة لقصة التوراة.

Chapter 2

خلق الإنسان

Chapter 2

Genesis 1–4

خلق الإنسان

يخلق الله السماوات والأرض، ويُكوِّن آدم وحواء على صورته، ويضعهما في الجنة. يكسر الإنسان الأول ثقة خالقه فيُطرَد إلى عالم تطبعه المشقة — وهي نقطة انطلاق كل قصة تأتي بعدها.

Chapter 3

نوح والطوفان والجيل التالي

Chapter 3

Genesis 6–9

نوح والطوفان والجيل التالي

حين يملأ العنف الأرض يحزن الله ويعزم على البدء من جديد. يجد نوح نعمة فيبني الفُلك. يأتي الطوفان ثم ينحسر، ويقيم الله عهده مع نوح، واضعًا قوسه في السحاب علامةً لكل جيل.

Chapter 4

عهد الرب مع إبراهيم

Chapter 4

Genesis 12, 15, 17

عهد الرب مع إبراهيم

يدعو الله أبرام للخروج من أرضه ويعده بأن يجعله أمة عظيمة تتبارك فيه جميع شعوب الأرض. ومن خلال رؤيا وعلامة الختان، يُثبِّت الله عهده مع إبراهيم ونسله.

Chapter 5

ولادة إسحاق

Chapter 5

Genesis 18, 21

ولادة إسحاق

بعد أن فقد إبراهيم وسارة كل أمل في الأولاد، يفتقدهما الرب ويُجدِّد وعده. تضحك سارة، لكن في الوقت المعيَّن يُولد إسحاق — ابن الموعد.

Chapter 6

امتحان إبراهيم

Chapter 6

Genesis 22

امتحان إبراهيم

يمتحن الله إيمان إبراهيم آمرًا إياه أن يقدِّم ابنه الوحيد إسحاق على جبل المُريَّا. حين يرفع إبراهيم السكين يتدخَّل الرب ويُعدُّ كبشًا بدلًا من إسحاق — صورة محورية للثقة والذبيحة وعناية الله.

Chapter 7

حلم يوسف

Chapter 7

Genesis 37

حلم يوسف

يحلم يوسف، ابن يعقوب المحبوب، أن أهله سيركعون أمامه يومًا. تفور غيرة إخوته فيبيعونه عبدًا إلى مصر — بداية رحلة عناية إلهية طويلة ستصون عائلة الموعد.

Chapter 8

يوسف وامرأة فوطيفار

Chapter 8

Genesis 39

يوسف وامرأة فوطيفار

في مصر يرتقي يوسف إلى مكانة الثقة في بيت فوطيفار. تتهمه زوجة فوطيفار زورًا بعد أن يرفض إغراءها، فيُلقى في السجن — لكنّ الرب يبقى معه.

Chapter 9

إخوة يوسف ينزلون إلى مصر

Chapter 9

Genesis 41–45

إخوة يوسف ينزلون إلى مصر

بعد سنوات يصير يوسف حاكمًا على مصر. حين يدفع الجوع إخوته إلى النزول من كنعان طلبًا للقمح، يقفون من غير أن يدروا أمام الأخ الذي خانوه. يكشف يوسف عن نفسه ويعفو عنهم، فتجتمع عائلة إسرائيل وتستقر في مصر.

Chapter 10

بنو إسرائيل تحت الاضطهاد

Chapter 10

Exodus 1–2

بنو إسرائيل تحت الاضطهاد

تمضي أجيال ويقوم فرعون جديد لا يعرف يوسف. يكثر العبرانيون فيُساقون إلى عبودية مُرَّة. ومن بينهم يُخبأ صبي عبراني اسمه موسى بين القصب، فيكبر في بيت فرعون نفسه.

Chapter 11

موسى والعليقة المشتعلة

Chapter 11

Exodus 3–4

موسى والعليقة المشتعلة

بعد فراره من مصر يرعى موسى الغنم في مديان. على جبل حوريب يظهر له الرب في عليقة تشتعل من غير أن تحترق، ويُرسله إلى مصر ليُخرج شعبه من العبودية.

Chapter 12

الفصح والخروج وعهد سيناء

Chapter 12

Exodus 5–20 and beyond

الفصح والخروج وعهد سيناء

يواجه موسى فرعون، فتنزل الضربات على مصر ويُذبح حمل الفصح. يُعتَق إسرائيل ويعبر البحر الأحمر على اليابسة. في البرية يُعطيهم الله المنّ والسلوى، ويُسلِّمهم الوصايا العشر في سيناء، ويُجدِّد عهده مع شعبه — داعيًا إياهم إلى اختيار الحياة وأرض الموعد التي أمامهم.

يجتمع مجلس شيوخ اليهود ليروا كيف يمكنهم التخلص من يسوع. في هذه الأثناء، يجلس يسوع مع بقية أتباعه ويطلب منهم أن يصلوا ضد الإغراءات.\ \ يصل يهوذا إلى المجلس ويعد قطع الفضة. يذهب يسوع بمفرده ليصلي. يطلب من أبيه السماوي أن يزيل عنه عبء كأسه. لكنه يقول إنه يفضل أن تتم مشيئة الله لا مشيئته. بينما يواصل يسوع الصلاة، أصبح عرقه كقطرات دم كبيرة. ينهض من الصلاة ويعود إلى التلاميذ. لكنهم نائمون. يقترب منه حشد من اليهود. يقود يهوذا الطريق ويقترب من يسوع. يقبله على خده. يندفع التلاميذ إلى الأمام ويسألونه عما إذا كان عليهم الذهاب إلى المعركة. يركض بطرس إلى الأمام ويقطع أذن أحد الرجال. يشفي يسوع الرجل ويوقف الشجار. يسألهم لماذا جاءوا بالهراوات. ويتم القبض على يسوع.

يتعرض يسوع للضرب على يد حراس الهيكل. يأمر رجل الحراس بإحضار يسوع إلى المجلس.\ \ يدخل حنان وقيافا. تملأ الغرفة مجموعة من الرجال اليهود. يريدون معرفة ما إذا كان يسوع هو المسيح. يجاوب يسوع فقط أنه إذا أخبرهم، فلن يصدقه المجلس. يقول إن ابن الإنسان سيجلس عن يمين الله.\ \ يسألونه إن كان هو ابن الله. يجيب يسوع أنهم يقولون إنه كذلك. لا يعرفون كيف يفسرون إجابته. يقف أحدهم ويشهد. سمع الجميع إجاباته. يقرر المجلس أن يأخذوه إلى بيلاطس.

51. صلب يسوع

لوقا 23:32

يصلون إلى المكان الذي أُقيمت فيه الصلبان. يُربط الآخرون إلى صلبانهم. يُجرد يسوع من ثيابه ويُقاد إلى صليبه. يلقون به عليه. تعلو الصرخات بينما يتم تثبيت الآخرين على صلبانهم. \ \ يتم دق المسامير في معصمي يسوع وقدميه وهو يصرخ. ثم يتم نصب الصلبان ببطء بينما يسحب الرومان الحبال. يُرفع يسوع عالياً في الهواء. يعلق على الصليب، متعباً ومتألماً. يصلي من أجل الحشد. يطلب من الله أن يغفر لهم لأنهم لا يعرفون ماذا يفعلون.\ \ يتمتم الحشد عند أقدام الصليب. يعلق حنان وقيافاس أنه أنقذ الآخرين. يتساءلون لماذا لا ينقذ نفسه. يبدأ الحشد بالسخرية. يحثونه على إنقاذ نفسه. لكنه لا يفعل ذلك.

Mark 1

بداية الإنجيل

Mark 1

Mark 1

بداية الإنجيل

يوحنا المعمدان يُعدّ الطريق. يُعمَّد يسوع ويُجرَّب في البرية ويدعو تلاميذه الأوائل ويبدأ بالشفاء والتعليم في الجليل.

Mark 2

سلطان المغفرة والشفاء

Mark 2

Mark 2

سلطان المغفرة والشفاء

يشفي يسوع مفلوجًا أُنزل من السقف، ويدعو لاوي العشّار، ويدافع عن تلاميذه لأكلهم مع الخطاة وقطفهم السنابل في السبت.

Mark 3

اختيار الاثني عشر

Mark 3

Mark 3

اختيار الاثني عشر

يشفي يسوع في السبت ويختار اثني عشر رسولًا ويُتّهم بإخراج الشياطين بقوة بعلزبول. يُعيد تعريف عائلته الحقيقية.

Mark 4

الأمثال والعاصفة

Mark 4

Mark 4

الأمثال والعاصفة

يُعلّم يسوع بالأمثال: الزارع، والسراج، والبذار النامي، وحبة الخردل. يُهدّئ عاصفة شديدة على بحر الجليل.

Mark 5

سلطان على الشياطين والمرض والموت

Mark 5

Mark 5

سلطان على الشياطين والمرض والموت

يُخرج يسوع لجيونًا من الشياطين، ويشفي امرأة نازفة منذ اثنتي عشرة سنة، ويُقيم ابنة يايرس من الموت.

Mark 6

الرفض والإرسالية والمعجزات

Mark 6

Mark 6

الرفض والإرسالية والمعجزات

يُرفض يسوع في الناصرة ويُرسل الاثني عشر ويقتل هيرودس يوحنا المعمدان. يُطعم يسوع خمسة آلاف ويمشي على الماء.

Mark 7

التقاليد والطهارة الحقيقية

Mark 7

Mark 7

التقاليد والطهارة الحقيقية

يتحدّى يسوع تقاليد الفريسيين حول الغسل الطقسي، ويُعلّم أن النجاسة تأتي من الداخل، ويشفي ابنة المرأة السوريفينيقية.

Mark 8

اعتراف بطرس وطريق الصليب

Mark 8

Mark 8

اعتراف بطرس وطريق الصليب

يُطعم يسوع أربعة آلاف ويشفي رجلًا أعمى ويعترف بطرس بأنه المسيح. يبدأ يسوع بالتعليم عن آلامه وموته القادمين.

Mark 9

التجلّي والتعليم عن التلمذة

Mark 9

Mark 9

التجلّي والتعليم عن التلمذة

يتجلّى يسوع أمام بطرس ويعقوب ويوحنا. يشفي صبيًّا به روح نجس ويُعلّم عن الخدمة واجتناب الخطية.

Mark 10

التعليم في الطريق إلى أورشليم

Mark 10

Mark 10

التعليم في الطريق إلى أورشليم

يُعلّم يسوع عن الطلاق ويبارك الأطفال ويتحدّى الرجل الغني ويتنبّأ بموته مجدّدًا ويشفي بارتيماوس الأعمى قرب أريحا.

Mark 11

الدخول الانتصاري وتطهير الهيكل

Mark 11

Mark 11

الدخول الانتصاري وتطهير الهيكل

يدخل يسوع أورشليم على حمار وسط هتافات «أوصنّا»، ويلعن شجرة تين يابسة، ويطرد الصيارفة، ويُعلّم عن الإيمان.

Mark 12

أمثال ومواجهات في الهيكل

Mark 12

Mark 12

أمثال ومواجهات في الهيكل

مثل الكرّامين، وأسئلة عن الضرائب والقيامة، وأعظم الوصايا، وتقدمة الأرملة بفلسَيها.

Mark 13

خطاب جبل الزيتون

Mark 13

Mark 13

خطاب جبل الزيتون

يتنبّأ يسوع بخراب الهيكل ويصف علامات نهاية الأزمنة، حاثًّا أتباعه على السهر واليقظة.

Mark 14

العشاء الأخير وجثسيماني والقبض عليه

Mark 14

Mark 14

العشاء الأخير وجثسيماني والقبض عليه

امرأة تدهن يسوع بالطيب. يتناول عشاء الفصح ويصلّي بألم في جثسيماني ويُسلَّم من يهوذا ويُقبض عليه ويُحاكَم أمام السنهدرين.

Mark 15

المحاكمة والصلب

Mark 15

Mark 15

المحاكمة والصلب

يُقدَّم يسوع أمام بيلاطس ويُحكم عليه ويُستهزأ به ويُصلب بين لصّين. يُغطّي الظلام الأرض. يموت يسوع ويدفنه يوسف الرامي.

Mark 16

القيامة

Mark 16

Mark 16

القيامة

تأتي النسوة إلى القبر صباح الأحد باكرًا فيجدنه فارغًا. شابّ بثياب بيضاء يُخبرهنّ أن يسوع قام وسبقهم إلى الجليل.

يعود يوحنا والآخرون إلى الغرفة حيث اجتمع أتباع يسوع. يدخلون قائلين إن يسوع قد قام بالفعل. يقول يوحنا إن يسوع ظهر لسمعان على الطريق. يتحدث سمعان عن كيف أنهم لم يتعرفوا على يسوع في البداية.\ \ ولكن عندما جلسوا لتناول العشاء وكسر يسوع الخبز، عرفوا من هو.\ \ يقف يسوع في الغرفة معهم. يسألهم لماذا هم قلقون ومتشككون. يمد يديه ليروها. يشجعهم على لمسه ليثبت لهم أنه من لحم ودم. يمدون أيديهم ويلمسون يديه.

يعلّم يسوع تلاميذه أن يصلّوا: «أبانا، ليتقدس اسمك». ويخرج الشياطين بإصبع الله، وينطق بالويلات على الفريسيين الذين ينقّون خارج الكأس.

Luke 12

أحبّوا أعداءكم

Luke 12

Luke 12

أحبّوا أعداءكم

يحذّر يسوع من الرياء والطمع، ويحدّث عن غنيّ غبيّ تُطلَب نفسه في الليلة التي امتلأت فيها مخازنه. ويدعو أتباعه أن يتّكلوا على الآب الذي يقوت الغربان، وأن يكونوا مستعدين لمجيء ابن الإنسان.

Luke 13

إيمان قائد المئة وابن الأرملة

Luke 13

Luke 13

إيمان قائد المئة وابن الأرملة

يدعو يسوع الجميع إلى التوبة، ويشفي امرأة منحنية في السبت، ويشبّه الملكوت بحبة خردل. ويحضّ على الدخول من الباب الضيق، ويبكي على أورشليم، المدينة القاتلة الأنبياء.

Luke 14

يسوع ويوحنا المعمدان

Luke 14

Luke 14

يسوع ويوحنا المعمدان

على مائدة أحد الفريسيين يعلّم يسوع المدعوين أن يتّكئوا في الموضع الأخير، ويعلّم المضيفين أن يدعوا المساكين. ويحدّث عن عشاء عظيم يرفض مدعوّوه أن يأتوا، ويدعو التلاميذ أن يحسبوا النفقة.

Luke 15

امرأة خاطئة تدهن يسوع

Luke 15

Luke 15

امرأة خاطئة تدهن يسوع

للفريسيين المتذمرين يحدّث يسوع عن راعٍ يترك التسعة والتسعين ليجد الواحد، وعن امرأة تفتّش عن درهم مفقود. ويركض أب ليحتضن ابنه الضال العائد: «كان ضالًّا فوُجد».

Luke 16

الأمثال وتهدئة العاصفة

Luke 16

Luke 16

الأمثال وتهدئة العاصفة

يحدّث يسوع عن وكيل حكيم ويعلّم أنه لا يقدر أحد أن يخدم الله والمال معًا. ويتجاهل رجل غني المسكين لعازر عند بابه، فيجد الأمر منعكسًا فيما وراء القبر.

Luke 17

شفاء المجنون

Luke 17

Luke 17

شفاء المجنون

يشفي يسوع عشرة برص، فلا يرجع ليشكر إلا واحد — وهو سامري. ويعلّم أن ملكوت الله في وسطهم، ويتكلم عن اليوم الذي يُعلَن فيه ابن الإنسان.

Luke 18

فتاة تحتضر وامرأة تعاني

Luke 18

Luke 18

فتاة تحتضر وامرأة تعاني

يحدّث يسوع عن أرملة ينال إلحاحها لها الإنصاف، وعن عشّار سُمعت صلاته المتواضعة دون صلاة فريسي. ويقبل الأولاد الصغار، ويتحدّى رئيسًا غنيًا، ويعطي البصر لأعمى مستعطٍ قرب أريحا.

Luke 19

إرسال الاثني عشر واعتراف بطرس

Luke 19

Luke 19

إرسال الاثني عشر واعتراف بطرس

يدعو يسوع زكّا لينزل من الجميزة، فيأتي الخلاص إلى بيته. ويدخل أورشليم والجموع تهتف بالتسبيح، ويبكي على المدينة، ويطهّر الهيكل.

Luke 20

التجلّي والتوجّه إلى أورشليم

Luke 20

Luke 20

التجلّي والتوجّه إلى أورشليم

يتحدّى الرؤساء سلطان يسوع، فيجيبهم بمثل الكرّامين الأردياء. ويردّ فخاخهم عن جزية قيصر وعن القيامة إلى نحورهم.

Luke 21

ثمن الاتّباع وإرسال الاثنين والسبعين

Luke 21

Luke 21

ثمن الاتّباع وإرسال الاثنين والسبعين

يكرّم يسوع فلسَي أرملة فقيرة فوق كل عطايا الأغنياء. ويسبق فينبئ بخراب الهيكل وبمجيء ابن الإنسان، حاضًّا أتباعه أن يسهروا ويصلّوا.

Luke 22

السامري الصالح ومريم ومرثا

Luke 22

Luke 22

السامري الصالح ومريم ومرثا

يأكل يسوع الفصح مع رسله — «هذا هو جسدي الذي يُبذَل عنكم» — بينما يتفق يهوذا على أن يسلّمه. ويصلي في جهاد على جبل الزيتون، ويُقبَض عليه، وينكره بطرس ثلاث مرات.

Luke 23

التعليم عن الصلاة وآية يونان

Luke 23

Luke 23

التعليم عن الصلاة وآية يونان

لا يجد بيلاطس ولا هيرودس علّة في يسوع، لكن الجمع يطلب صلبه. وعلى الصليب يغفر يسوع لصالبيه، ويعد لصًّا يحتضر بالفردوس، ويستودع روحه في يدي الآب.

Luke 24

تحذيرات وتشجيعات

Luke 24

Luke 24

تحذيرات وتشجيعات

تجد النساء القبر فارغًا، ويعرف تلميذان يسوع القائم من الأموات عند كسر الخبز في عمواس. ويظهر يسوع للتلاميذ المجتمعين، ويفتح لهم الكتب، ثم يُصعَد إلى السماء.

1. The Beginning

Genesis 1:1

1. The Beginning

Genesis 1:1

The story of Jesus fits within the larger story of the Judeo Christian tradition. The purpose of everything since creation has been to point to the life of Jesus. All of creation speaks of the majesty of God. As God created man and woman he intended them to live in peace with him forever. But because of their disobedience mankind was separated from God. But God still loved mankind so throughout the Scriptures God reveals his plan to save the world.

3:43
2. Birth Of Jesus

Luke 1:1

2. Birth Of Jesus

Luke 1:1

Luke makes his introduction as the careful author of this Gospel. The angel Gabriel appears to Mary, a virgin in Nazareth. He announces to her that she has found favor with God and will give birth to Jesus, the Son of God. Through Jesus' birth, prophecies are fulfilled by the arrangement of events. God leaves no detail unnoticed. The same can be said of our own lives.

2:15
3. Childhood Of Jesus

Luke 2:21

3. Childhood Of Jesus

Luke 2:21

One week after the baby is born, He is circumcised and officially named Jesus. While Jesus is a small boy they go to the temple where they meet a man named Simeon. The Holy Spirit had assured Simeon he would not die before seeing the Lord's Messiah. Simeon sees Jesus and declares Him the promised Messiah.

3:47
4. Baptism Of Jesus By John

Luke 3:1

4. Baptism Of Jesus By John

Luke 3:1

John the Baptist calls out in the desert. He preaches by the river Jordan, "Turn away from your sins and be baptized, and God will forgive your sins." He is the one Isaiah predicted would make way for the Lord. The crowds gather. Immediately, he warns them not to only say they have repented. Instead, they're to follow repentance with actions that exhibit a changed heart. Jesus is baptized and receives the Holy Spirit. He kneels at the feet of someone lesser than Himself to be baptized. He demonstrates how we are to be humble.

2:22
5. The Devil Tempts Jesus

Luke 4:1

5. The Devil Tempts Jesus

Luke 4:1

After Jesus has been baptized, He's led by the Spirit into the desert. He spends 40 days there, constantly tempted by the devil. All that time, he eats nothing. The devil tries to tempt Jesus, but Jesus answers using Scripture, resisting him.

3:07
6. Jesus Proclaims Fulfillment Of The Scriptures

Luke 4:14

6. Jesus Proclaims Fulfillment Of The Scriptures

Luke 4:14

When Jesus returns to Nazareth, He goes to the synagogue. He's asked to read the Scriptures and is handed the Book of Isaiah. From it, He reads Isaiah 61:1-2. The prophecy speaks of bringing good news to the poor, proclaiming liberty to the captives, recovery of sight to the blind, freeing the oppressed, and announcing that it's time the Lord will save His people. When He finishes reading, Jesus announces to the people that the prophecy has come true as it was just read.

1:02
7. Parable Of The Pharisee And Tax Collector

Luke 18:9

7. Parable Of The Pharisee And Tax Collector

Luke 18:9

Jesus teaches from a boat off the shore of Lake Gennesaret. He speaks in parables, giving the example of a Pharisee and tax collector going to the temple to pray. The two men approach prayer very differently. The Pharisee in the story stands by himself and lists his respectable attributes. He thanks God that he is not greedy, dishonest, or an adulterer like everyone else. He specifically points out the tax collector and thanks God for not being like him. The Pharisee boldly tells God what he does: He fasts two days a week and gives a tenth of his income. The tax collector stands at a distance from the altar. Head bowed, he beats on his chest. The only thing he prays is, "God, have pity on me, a sinner!"

2:01
8. Miraculous Catch Of Fish

Luke 5:1

8. Miraculous Catch Of Fish

Luke 5:1

Jesus tells the fisherman who owns it to push out farther and let down their nets. The fisherman grumbles that he and the others have already been out all night long. They didn't catch anything. The fisherman agrees to go out and calls to his partners. Jesus sits in the boat with the fisherman. He waits expectantly. Then gathers the nets, slowly bringing something to the surface. He laughs with joy when he sees the nets are full of flopping fish. When they're done, the fisherman sits in a boat full of fish. He looks up to Jesus. The fisherman frowns and says, "Go away from me, Lord. I am a sinful man." Jesus tells him not to be afraid, that from then on, he would be a fisher of men.

2:14
9. Jairuss Daughter Brought Back To Life

Luke 8:41

9. Jairuss Daughter Brought Back To Life

Luke 8:41

Crowds press in on Jesus as He leaves the synagogue. One voice rises above the others. A man, Jairus, begs Jesus to save his sick, 12-year-old daughter. Another man runs up to Jairus. He tells him not to bother the teacher, that his daughter has died. Jesus turns and tells him not to be afraid. And that if Jairus would believe, his daughter would be well. Jesus and the disciples visit the family. The neighbors wail for the loss of the daughter. She lies lifeless on a cot. Jesus looks at her for a moment. Then He looks to the child’s mother and comforts her. He says the child isn't dead, but that she’s actually just asleep. Jesus sits and looks at the girl for a moment, then tells her to rise.

3:10
10. Disciples Chosen

Luke 5:27

10. Disciples Chosen

Luke 5:27

Jesus spots a tax collector named Matthew Levi at the gate. He collects toll money for customs as people pass through. As Jesus looks at him, Matthew senses it and looks up. Jesus says, "Follow me." Matthew watches Him go for a moment. Silently, he stands and leaves everything to follow Jesus. Later Jesus goes up a hill to pray. He prays the entire night to God. When He comes down from the hill the next morning, He gathers His followers. From them, he chooses 12 apostles. Simon (who Jesus named Peter) and Simon's brother Andrew had been the fishermen who experienced the miracle of a large catch of fish. Then Jesus chooses James and John, Philip and Bartholomew. And He chooses Matthew, the tax collector he had called at the gate. And finally Jesus chooses Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who would betray Jesus.

11. Beatitudes

Luke 6:20

11. Beatitudes

Luke 6:20

Jesus looks out over the crowds gathered to hear him speak. But instead of speaking to the masses, Jesus turns back to his disciples. He encourages them for the journey ahead. He assures them that they are blessed when people hate them, reject them, insult them, and say that they are evil because they follow Jesus. He encourages them to be happy and dance for joy when that happens. Because there will be great reward in heaven for them. And He reminds them that their ancestors acted the same way toward prophets.

3:39

يبشّر الملاك جبرائيل زكريا بميلاد يوحنا المعمدان المزمع، ويبشّر مريم العذراء بميلاد يسوع. فترنّم مريم بتسبيح الله، ويولد يوحنا لأليصابات في شيخوختها.

أحبّوا أعداءكم

Luke 12

Luke 12

أحبّوا أعداءكم

إيمان قائد المئة وابن الأرملة

يسوع ويوحنا المعمدان

Luke 14

يسوع ويوحنا المعمدان

على مائدة أحد الفريسيين يعلّم يسوع المدعوين أن يتّكئوا في الموضع الأخير، ويعلّم المضيفين أن يدعوا المساكين. ويحدّث عن عشاء عظيم يرفض مدعوّوه أن يأتوا، ويدعو التلاميذ أن يحسبوا النفقة.

امرأة خاطئة تدهن يسوع

Luke 15

امرأة خاطئة تدهن يسوع

شفاء المجنون

شفاء المجنون

يشفي يسوع عشرة برص، فلا يرجع ليشكر إلا واحد — وهو سامري. ويعلّم أن ملكوت الله في وسطهم، ويتكلم عن اليوم الذي يُعلَن فيه ابن الإنسان.

فتاة تحتضر وامرأة تعاني

فتاة تحتضر وامرأة تعاني

يحدّث يسوع عن أرملة ينال إلحاحها لها الإنصاف، وعن عشّار سُمعت صلاته المتواضعة دون صلاة فريسي. ويقبل الأولاد الصغار، ويتحدّى رئيسًا غنيًا، ويعطي البصر لأعمى مستعطٍ قرب أريحا.

إرسال الاثني عشر واعتراف بطرس

إرسال الاثني عشر واعتراف بطرس

التجلّي والتوجّه إلى أورشليم

يتحدّى الرؤساء سلطان يسوع، فيجيبهم بمثل الكرّامين الأردياء. ويردّ فخاخهم عن جزية قيصر وعن القيامة إلى نحورهم.

Luke 21

ثمن الاتّباع وإرسال الاثنين والسبعين

Luke 21

Luke 21

ثمن الاتّباع وإرسال الاثنين والسبعين

يكرّم يسوع فلسَي أرملة فقيرة فوق كل عطايا الأغنياء. ويسبق فينبئ بخراب الهيكل وبمجيء ابن الإنسان، حاضًّا أتباعه أن يسهروا ويصلّوا.

Luke 22

السامري الصالح ومريم ومرثا

Luke 22

Luke 22

السامري الصالح ومريم ومرثا

يأكل يسوع الفصح مع رسله — «هذا هو جسدي الذي يُبذَل عنكم» — بينما يتفق يهوذا على أن يسلّمه. ويصلي في جهاد على جبل الزيتون، ويُقبَض عليه، وينكره بطرس ثلاث مرات.

Luke 23

التعليم عن الصلاة وآية يونان

Luke 23

Luke 23

التعليم عن الصلاة وآية يونان

لا يجد بيلاطس ولا هيرودس علّة في يسوع، لكن الجمع يطلب صلبه. وعلى الصليب يغفر يسوع لصالبيه، ويعد لصًّا يحتضر بالفردوس، ويستودع روحه في يدي الآب.

Luke 24

تحذيرات وتشجيعات

Luke 24

Luke 24

تحذيرات وتشجيعات

تجد النساء القبر فارغًا، ويعرف تلميذان يسوع القائم من الأموات عند كسر الخبز في عمواس. ويظهر يسوع للتلاميذ المجتمعين، ويفتح لهم الكتب، ثم يُصعَد إلى السماء.

1. The Beginning

Genesis 1:1

1. The Beginning

Genesis 1:1

The story of Jesus fits within the larger story of the Judeo Christian tradition. The purpose of everything since creation has been to point to the life of Jesus. All of creation speaks of the majesty of God. As God created man and woman he intended them to live in peace with him forever. But because of their disobedience mankind was separated from God. But God still loved mankind so throughout the Scriptures God reveals his plan to save the world.

3:43
2. Birth Of Jesus

Luke 1:1

2. Birth Of Jesus

Luke 1:1

Luke makes his introduction as the careful author of this Gospel. The angel Gabriel appears to Mary, a virgin in Nazareth. He announces to her that she has found favor with God and will give birth to Jesus, the Son of God. Through Jesus' birth, prophecies are fulfilled by the arrangement of events. God leaves no detail unnoticed. The same can be said of our own lives.

2:15
3. Childhood Of Jesus

Luke 2:21

3. Childhood Of Jesus

Luke 2:21

One week after the baby is born, He is circumcised and officially named Jesus. While Jesus is a small boy they go to the temple where they meet a man named Simeon. The Holy Spirit had assured Simeon he would not die before seeing the Lord's Messiah. Simeon sees Jesus and declares Him the promised Messiah.

4. Baptism Of Jesus By John

Luke 3:1

4. Baptism Of Jesus By John

Luke 3:1

John the Baptist calls out in the desert. He preaches by the river Jordan, "Turn away from your sins and be baptized, and God will forgive your sins." He is the one Isaiah predicted would make way for the Lord. The crowds gather. Immediately, he warns them not to only say they have repented. Instead, they're to follow repentance with actions that exhibit a changed heart. Jesus is baptized and receives the Holy Spirit. He kneels at the feet of someone lesser than Himself to be baptized. He demonstrates how we are to be humble.

5. The Devil Tempts Jesus

Luke 4:1

5. The Devil Tempts Jesus

Luke 4:1

After Jesus has been baptized, He's led by the Spirit into the desert. He spends 40 days there, constantly tempted by the devil. All that time, he eats nothing. The devil tries to tempt Jesus, but Jesus answers using Scripture, resisting him.

6. Jesus Proclaims Fulfillment Of The Scriptures

Luke 4:14

6. Jesus Proclaims Fulfillment Of The Scriptures

Luke 4:14

When Jesus returns to Nazareth, He goes to the synagogue. He's asked to read the Scriptures and is handed the Book of Isaiah. From it, He reads Isaiah 61:1-2. The prophecy speaks of bringing good news to the poor, proclaiming liberty to the captives, recovery of sight to the blind, freeing the oppressed, and announcing that it's time the Lord will save His people. When He finishes reading, Jesus announces to the people that the prophecy has come true as it was just read.

7. Parable Of The Pharisee And Tax Collector

Luke 18:9

7. Parable Of The Pharisee And Tax Collector

Luke 18:9

Jesus teaches from a boat off the shore of Lake Gennesaret. He speaks in parables, giving the example of a Pharisee and tax collector going to the temple to pray. The two men approach prayer very differently. The Pharisee in the story stands by himself and lists his respectable attributes. He thanks God that he is not greedy, dishonest, or an adulterer like everyone else. He specifically points out the tax collector and thanks God for not being like him. The Pharisee boldly tells God what he does: He fasts two days a week and gives a tenth of his income. The tax collector stands at a distance from the altar. Head bowed, he beats on his chest. The only thing he prays is, "God, have pity on me, a sinner!"

8. Miraculous Catch Of Fish

Luke 5:1

8. Miraculous Catch Of Fish

Luke 5:1

Jesus tells the fisherman who owns it to push out farther and let down their nets. The fisherman grumbles that he and the others have already been out all night long. They didn't catch anything. The fisherman agrees to go out and calls to his partners. Jesus sits in the boat with the fisherman. He waits expectantly. Then gathers the nets, slowly bringing something to the surface. He laughs with joy when he sees the nets are full of flopping fish. When they're done, the fisherman sits in a boat full of fish. He looks up to Jesus. The fisherman frowns and says, "Go away from me, Lord. I am a sinful man." Jesus tells him not to be afraid, that from then on, he would be a fisher of men.

9. Jairuss Daughter Brought Back To Life

Luke 8:41

9. Jairuss Daughter Brought Back To Life

Luke 8:41

Crowds press in on Jesus as He leaves the synagogue. One voice rises above the others. A man, Jairus, begs Jesus to save his sick, 12-year-old daughter. Another man runs up to Jairus. He tells him not to bother the teacher, that his daughter has died. Jesus turns and tells him not to be afraid. And that if Jairus would believe, his daughter would be well. Jesus and the disciples visit the family. The neighbors wail for the loss of the daughter. She lies lifeless on a cot. Jesus looks at her for a moment. Then He looks to the child’s mother and comforts her. He says the child isn't dead, but that she’s actually just asleep. Jesus sits and looks at the girl for a moment, then tells her to rise.

10. Disciples Chosen

Luke 5:27

10. Disciples Chosen

Luke 5:27

Jesus spots a tax collector named Matthew Levi at the gate. He collects toll money for customs as people pass through. As Jesus looks at him, Matthew senses it and looks up. Jesus says, "Follow me." Matthew watches Him go for a moment. Silently, he stands and leaves everything to follow Jesus. Later Jesus goes up a hill to pray. He prays the entire night to God. When He comes down from the hill the next morning, He gathers His followers. From them, he chooses 12 apostles. Simon (who Jesus named Peter) and Simon's brother Andrew had been the fishermen who experienced the miracle of a large catch of fish. Then Jesus chooses James and John, Philip and Bartholomew. And He chooses Matthew, the tax collector he had called at the gate. And finally Jesus chooses Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Simon the Zealot, Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who would betray Jesus.

11. Beatitudes

Luke 6:20

11. Beatitudes

Luke 6:20

Jesus looks out over the crowds gathered to hear him speak. But instead of speaking to the masses, Jesus turns back to his disciples. He encourages them for the journey ahead. He assures them that they are blessed when people hate them, reject them, insult them, and say that they are evil because they follow Jesus. He encourages them to be happy and dance for joy when that happens. Because there will be great reward in heaven for them. And He reminds them that their ancestors acted the same way toward prophets.

Luke 6:24

12. Sermon On The Mount

Luke 6:24

Jesus turns to the crowds and walks through them, teaching. He advises everyone how to walk through life in love. And talks of how, out of pride, we often judge others. He implores those who are listening to love their enemies, to actively pray for them. He speaks of offering more than what is asked of you. Do for others what you would have them do for you.

13. Blessed Are Those Who Hear And Obey

Luke 11:27

Jesus reminds us that those who hear and obey are blessed.

14. Sinful Woman Forgiven

Luke 7:36

A Pharisee invites Jesus to have dinner at His house. They're eating when a woman approaches Jesus. Everyone in the house stares, including the Pharisee. Jesus tells the Pharisee a story. He says that there were two men who owed money to someone. One owed 500 silver coins. The other owed 50. Neither men could pay their debt. So the lender canceled both debts. 15. Women Disciples

Luke 8:1

Jesus continues through the countryside. He's adamant in preaching the good news about the kingdom of God. The twelve disciples follow him. And some women follow as well. They serve the disciples, using their own resources to aid the ministry of Jesus.

16. John The Baptist In Prison

Luke 7:1

Herod has thrown John the Baptist into prison. Messengers come to him in the prison. They relay to him all that Jesus has been doing. 17. Parable Of The Sower And The Seed

Luke 8:4

The crowds press in on Jesus as He walks and teaches. He tells a parable of someone sowing seeds of grain in a field. The seed falls in a number of places, each representing something to the crowd. A disciple asks Jesus why He speaks in parables. Jesus explains the parable to the disciples. The seed that's scattered is the Word of God.

18. Parable Of The Lamp

Luke 11:33

Jesus uses a torch to explain how his followers should live. No one covers the light or puts it under a bed. Instead, they put it in a place where people will see the light when they come in. He goes on to say that whatever is kept a secret will be brought into the open. And anything that's covered up will be found and brought into the light.

19. Jesus Calms The Storm

Luke 8:22

Jesus gets into a boat and tells His disciples they should all go to the other side of the lake. Along the way, Jesus falls asleep. A storm starts to rage. Waves stretch high over the bow. And the boat starts to take on water. The whole time, Jesus stays asleep. The disciples hold on tight. They try to keep the boat afloat. Finally, Peter cries out to the still sleeping Jesus. He tells Jesus that the boat is taking on water and that they'll all be drowned. Jesus stands and puts a hand out toward the storm. The storm clears. And the seas immediately calm.

20. Healing Of The Demoniac

Luke 8:26

Jesus and His disciples continue to sail and arrive at Gerasa. A wild man on the shore growls at their approach. Jesus hurries toward him, ahead of His disciples. The man threatens Jesus with the rock. But Jesus just continues to stare at him. The man calls Jesus by name and declares Him to be the Son of God. Jesus asks him his name. At first the man won't say. But Jesus holds out a hand to him. He says his name is Legion. He begs not to be sent back to the abyss. Instead, he wants to go into a nearby herd of pigs. Jesus puts a hand out to the pigs.

21. Jesus Feeds 5000

Luke 9:1

Jesus and the disciples continue to walk the countryside. And a great crowd follows them. Peter comes and asks Jesus to send the people away. Jesus takes the baskets and proclaims to the heavens and the people, "Blessed is the Lord God, King of the Universe who brings forth bread from the earth."

Jesus asks who the crowds say He is. Peter speaks up immediately. He claims that some in the crowds say Jesus is John the Baptist. Others say He's Elijah. 23. The Transfiguration

23. The Transfiguration

Luke 9:28

يدعو يسوع الجميع إلى التوبة، ويشفي امرأة منحنية في السبت، ويشبّه الملكوت بحبة خردل. ويحضّ على الدخول من الباب الضيق، ويبكي على أورشليم، المدينة القاتلة الأنبياء.

يسوع ويوحنا المعمدان

امرأة خاطئة تدهن يسوع

للفريسيين المتذمرين يحدّث يسوع عن راعٍ يترك التسعة والتسعين ليجد الواحد، وعن امرأة تفتّش عن درهم مفقود. ويركض أب ليحتضن ابنه الضال العائد: «كان ضالًّا فوُجد».

شفاء المجنون

تجد النساء القبر فارغًا، ويعرف تلميذان يسوع القائم من الأموات عند كسر الخبز في عمواس. ويظهر يسوع للتلاميذ المجتمعين، ويفتح لهم الكتب، ثم يُصعَد إلى السماء.

يسوع يحمل عارضة صليبه عبر الشوارع. الحرس الروماني يضربون من يعترض طريقهم. يسوع يواصل الكفاح تحت ثقل الصليب.\ \ ينهار في الشارع، ويسقط على ركبتيه. حارس روماني ينظر إلى الحشد ويرى رجلاً ضخمًا. يُجبر على حمل الصليب بينما يتعثر يسوع في طريقه. الحشود تصرخ بغضب. لكن البعض يبكي.\ \ يسوع يحثهم على البكاء على أنفسهم لأن هناك أوقاتًا أصعب قادمة. يدفع الرومان يسوع وراءهم، ويحثونه على المضي قدماً عندما يتوقف أو يتعثر.

51. صلب يسوع

يصلون إلى المكان الذي أُقيمت فيه الصلبان. يُربط الآخرون إلى صلبانهم. يُجرد يسوع من ثيابه ويُقاد إلى صليبه. يلقون به عليه. تعلو الصرخات بينما يتم تثبيت الآخرين على صلبانهم. \ \ يتم دق المسامير في معصمي يسوع وقدميه وهو يصرخ. ثم يتم نصب الصلبان ببطء بينما يسحب الرومان الحبال. يُرفع يسوع عالياً في الهواء. يعلق على الصليب، متعباً ومتألماً. يصلي من أجل الحشد. يطلب من الله أن يغفر لهم لأنهم لا يعرفون ماذا يفعلون.\ \ يتمتم الحشد عند أقدام الصليب. يعلق حنان وقيافاس أنه أنقذ الآخرين. يتساءلون لماذا لا ينقذ نفسه. يبدأ الحشد بالسخرية. يحثونه على إنقاذ نفسه. لكنه لا يفعل ذلك.

مريم المجدلية تندفع إلى غرفة مليئة بالتلاميذ. تخبر الرجال أن الحجر قد دُحرج. وأنها عندما دخلت هي والآخرون القبر، كان الجسد قد اختفى.\ \ تتحدث جوانا عن الملائكة. تقول إن هناك رجلين متألقين. وأخبروا النساء ألا يبحثن عن الأحياء بين الأموات.\ \ يسرع بطرس إلى القبر. يدخل راكضًا ويمشي مباشرة إلى الرف الصخري. لكن لا يوجد جسد. لا يوجد سوى الكتان. يركع ويأخذه بيديه. يقلبه، وينظر من خلاله. لكنه توقف بعد لحظة. تنهد وأحنى رأسه.

يعود يوحنا والآخرون إلى الغرفة حيث اجتمع أتباع يسوع. يدخلون قائلين إن يسوع قد قام بالفعل. يقول يوحنا إن يسوع ظهر لسمعان على الطريق. يتحدث سمعان عن كيف أنهم لم يتعرفوا على يسوع في البداية.\ \ ولكن عندما جلسوا لتناول العشاء وكسر يسوع الخبز، عرفوا من هو.\ \ يقف يسوع في الغرفة معهم. يسألهم لماذا هم قلقون ومتشككون. يمد يديه ليروها. يشجعهم على لمسه ليثبت لهم أنه من لحم ودم. يمدون أيديهم ويلمسون يديه.

he Medici Oriental Press Arabic Gospels of 1590-1591 is the first substantial Arabic book printed in Europe from movable type and the most accomplished example of Robert Granjon's Arabic typography. For the full account of Pope Gregory XIII's 1584 commission, Cardinal Ferdinando de' Medici's patronage, and Giovanni Battista Raimondi's direction of the press at Rome, see the canonical entry at Arabic-1591-Typographia-Medicea-Gospels-Original.

The edition exists in two issues. The 1590 printing carries the Arabic text alone across 464 folio pages and was prepared for distribution to Arabic-speaking Christian communities in Egypt, Syria, and Mount Lebanon through Maronite and Melkite contacts. The 1591 issue adds an interlinear Latin Vulgate translation by Antonius Sionita and was intended for European scholarly readers. Both issues use the same Granjon naskh type cut at Rome between 1583 and 1586, together with sixty-seven woodcut Gospel scenes by Antonio Tempesta that were reused in 1619 for a Syriac New Testament. The Arabic text is the Alexandrian Vulgate recension. It descends ultimately from a ninth-century translation made from the Greek at the monasteries of Palestine and Sinai.

Raimondi imported Arabic manuscripts from Aleppo, Cairo, and Istanbul to establish copy-text and cut the first matrices that could render the full range of ligatures required for classical Arabic. Granjon produced three sizes. The press issued Euclid, Avicenna, and Arabic grammars alongside the Gospels. Sales were poor. The Medici Press closed in 1610, its matrices sold to the Stamperia Orientale Romana and eventually to the Propaganda Fide. The Arabic Gospels remained the standard printed Arabic New Testament among Catholic missions until the Propaganda edition of 1671 (Jones 1994, pp. 94-98).

itab Zabur Dawud al-nabi, the Book of the Psalms of David the Prophet, is an Arabic Psalter produced around 1600 in the eastern Mediterranean, likely in Ottoman Egypt or Syria, where Melkite, Coptic, and Syriac Orthodox communities maintained parallel Arabic Psalter traditions for liturgical use. The text follows the Septuagint numbering of the psalms used across the Christian East, with the additional Psalm 151 preserved at the end.

Arabic translations of the Psalter circulated among Arabic-speaking Christians from the eighth century. By the late medieval period, several recensions coexisted: one from the Syriac Peshitta used by the Melkites, one from the Greek Septuagint used in Egypt, and a revised version attributed to al-Harith ibn Sinan of the ninth century (Graf 1944, vol. 1). The title's honorific for David, al-nabi with the pious formula of salutation, reflects the Islamic environment in which this manuscript tradition was copied and read. Arabic Psalters were among the most frequently transcribed biblical books in the Arabic Christian tradition, used in private devotion and monastic recitation (Griffith 2013, pp. 171-174). The copy preserves a clear naskh script on paper.

his Arabic Gospel manuscript dated 1687 was copied by the scribe Zacharia and contains the four Gospels in an Arabic translation of the kind that circulated among Christian Arabic-speaking communities of Egypt and Syria in the Mamluk and Ottoman periods. The text belongs to the family of Arabic Gospels translated from Greek and Syriac Vorlagen, often produced in Coptic or Melkite monastic scriptoria and copied down the centuries for liturgical and catechetical use (Metzger 1977, pp. 257-268).

Arabic translations of the Gospels exist in at least a dozen distinct textual families identified by Hikmat Kashouh, ranging from early translations of the eighth and ninth centuries through Alexandrian Vulgate revisions of the thirteenth. Manuscripts of the seventeenth century typically transmit the Alexandrian Vulgate recension, which had stabilized by the late medieval period and remained in use in Coptic Orthodox liturgy.

The manuscript was digitized by the Bayerische Staatsbibliothek in Munich through the World Digital Library project, whose collections were absorbed by the Library of Congress. Without direct codicological study the precise Arabic family and provenance of the Zacharia Gospels cannot be determined, but the date and scribe's name establish it within the continuing tradition of Eastern Christian Arabic scriptoria.

his Coptic-Arabic Gospel of John of about 1700 is one of a series of bilingual manuscripts produced for the Coptic Orthodox Church of Egypt in which the Bohairic Coptic text stands in parallel columns with an Arabic translation. By the end of the first millennium, spoken Coptic had largely given way to Arabic as the daily language of Egyptian Christians, and liturgical manuscripts from the thirteenth century onward routinely supplied Arabic alongside Coptic so that the congregation could follow the reading.

The Bohairic dialect, spoken historically in the Nile Delta, became the liturgical standard of the Coptic Church after the eleventh century. his bilingual Coptic-Arabic Gospel of Luke from about 1700 sets the Bohairic Coptic text in one column against an Arabic translation in the facing column. Such bilingual Gospels were produced for the Coptic Orthodox Church of Egypt from the medieval period onward, as Arabic had replaced Coptic as the spoken language of Egyptian Christians by the end of the first millennium.

The Bohairic dialect of Lower Egypt had become the liturgical standard of the Coptic Church by the eleventh century, displacing the Sahidic of Upper Egypt. Arabic Gospel texts in such manuscripts typically preserve the Alexandrian Vulgate recension, a thirteenth-century textual standardization drawn from earlier Arabic translations that themselves descended from Greek, Syriac, and Coptic originals (Metzger 1977, pp. 257-268). Kashouh's classification identifies over twenty distinct families within the Arabic Gospel tradition.

The manuscript was digitized by the Bayerische Staatsbibliothek in Munich through the World Digital Library and is now accessible through the Library of Congress. It forms part of a set with the John and Mark manuscripts in the same collection, likely originating from a single Egyptian monastic scriptorium.

manuscript of the historical books of the Old Testament in Arabic, dated 1748, cataloged by the World Digital Library as item 11345 and preserved within the Coptic Orthodox tradition. Arabic Bible translation within the Coptic Church developed from the ninth century onward as spoken Coptic gave way to Arabic among Christian communities in Egypt, and by the medieval centuries most Coptic lectionaries circulated bilingually with Arabic translations keyed to the Bohairic Coptic text (Griffith in Bailey 2013).

The Arabic of Coptic Old Testament books of this period typically translates not from the Hebrew but from the Septuagint as mediated through Coptic, with occasional correction against Syriac and Greek manuscripts available in Egyptian monastic libraries. The corpus, along with the wider Christian Arabic tradition, was catalogued comprehensively by Georg Graf in his five-volume Geschichte der christlichen arabischen Literatur (Graf 1944-53), which remains the reference for tracing individual manuscripts to their textual families.

The 1748 date on the Washington copy places it in the late Ottoman period of Coptic scribal activity, when monasteries such as Saint Anthony in the Eastern Desert and Saint Macarius in the Wadi al-Natrun continued to copy biblical, liturgical, and patristic texts for parish use. Identification of the specific scriptorium and codicological features awaits further examination.

l-'Unwān al-'ajīb fī ru'yā al-ḥabīb (The Wondrous Title on the Revelation of the Beloved), a manuscript Arabic commentary on the Book of Revelation by Yūsuf al-Bānī, dated 1789 (1204 AH). The title frames the Apocalypse as the ru'yā of the beloved disciple John. The text combines translation of the Greek Apocalypse with a verse-by-verse commentary in Arabic, drawing on earlier Melkite and Coptic Arabic exegesis of the book.

Arabic Christian commentary on Revelation had been relatively sparse before the eighteenth century compared with the commentary tradition on the Gospels and Pauline Epistles. Graf's Geschichte der christlichen arabischen Literatur notes al-Bānī among the late-eighteenth-century Arabic Christian scribes working in the Melkite orbit under Ottoman rule (Graf 1951, Vol. 4).

The manuscript preserves one branch of the Arabic reception of the final book of the New Testament at the close of the Ottoman eighteenth century, before the missionary Arabic printings of the nineteenth century (Shidyaq, Van Dyck, Jesuit editions) standardized the vocabulary for Apocalyptic terms.

his manuscript, formerly catalogued by the World Digital Library as item 11342 and preserved at the Walters Art Museum as W.592, contains the Pentateuch in Arabic as used by the Coptic Orthodox Church of Egypt. The volume dates to around 1800 and transmits a translation rooted in the medieval Copto-Arabic tradition, where the Arabic rendering was produced from or corrected against the Bohairic Coptic.

Arabic became the liturgical and scholarly language of Egyptian Christians after the Fatimid and Ayyubid centuries. By the thirteenth century Copto-Arabic biblical manuscripts routinely presented parallel Coptic and Arabic columns or Arabic alone. The 1800 date places this codex at the end of the long Ottoman copying tradition in Egypt, shortly before European missionary societies began introducing printed Arabic scripture into the Coptic community.

The title وخمست أسفار من التوراة, the Five Books of the Torah, uses the Arabic term tawrah familiar from the Qur'an rather than the neologisms later adopted by Protestant translators. Graf treats the Copto-Arabic Pentateuch transmission in his Geschichte der christlichen arabischen Literatur, identifying a chain of manuscripts running from the thirteenth through the nineteenth centuries. The Walters copy preserves the text in a naskh hand at the end of that transmission.

he Smith-Van Dyck Arabic Bible is the standard Arabic Protestant Scripture of the modern era. The complete translation was published at Beirut by the American Mission Press in 1865, with the New Testament appearing first in 1860. The 1867 printing represents one of the early full-Bible editions issued after the initial release. The translation was made from Hebrew and Greek into Classical Arabic with attention to the contemporary literary norms of the Nahda, the Arab cultural awakening then underway in Syria and Egypt.

Eli Smith of the American Board of Commissioners for Foreign Missions began the project in 1847 after preliminary study of the earlier Arabic translations, including the seventeenth-century London Polyglot Arabic, the Propaganda Fide version of 1671, and the Roman Catholic Carshuni manuscripts. He assembled an editorial team of Syrian Christian scholars in Beirut: Butrus al-Bustani, a Maronite-born Protestant convert who became the leading Arabic lexicographer of the century, and Nasif al-Yaziji, a Greek Orthodox man of letters whose mastery of Classical Arabic style was widely acknowledged. Smith died in 1857 with only the Pentateuch complete. Cornelius Van Alen Van Dyck, a medical missionary and linguist, took over the project in 1857 and completed the Old Testament in 1864. Sheikh Yusuf al-Asir, a Muslim scholar of Azhar training, provided final editorial review of the Arabic style.

The American Mission Press at Beirut cut its own Arabic font specifically for the translation. The type, designed by Smith himself and the calligrapher Halil Dib of Beirut, combined the legibility needed for printed text with fidelity to the naskh tradition. It was widely copied by other Arabic presses in the late nineteenth century.

The first Beirut edition of the complete Bible of 1865 was priced for wide distribution. The British and Foreign Bible Society and the American Bible Society took over print runs from the American Mission Press and distributed the translation across the Arab world through their agencies in Beirut, Alexandria, Cairo, Baghdad, and Istanbul. By 1900 the Van Dyck text had become the most widely read Arabic Bible, read not only by Protestants but increasingly by Orthodox, Melkite, and even some Coptic communities.

The translation shaped modern literary Arabic alongside the other Nahda projects of al-Bustani and the Zaidan family. Its vocabulary for Christian theology entered Protestant Arab church life and, through its wide circulation, established common phrasing for biblical quotation in Arabic journalism and literature of the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

The Van Dyck Bible remains in active use. A modest revision undertaken by the Bible Society in Lebanon in the 1980s adjusted archaic spellings and clarified some grammar, but the 1865 text remains the base. For many Arab Christian communities it is the Bible their great-grandparents read, heard in church, and copied by hand when printed copies were scarce.

his codex is a handwritten Arabic New Testament dated 1908. Its scribe, patron, and precise place of production have not been identified, and no colophon transcribed from the manuscript has yet been published. The book belongs to a tradition of hand-copied Arab Christian Scripture that continued in Ottoman Syria, Egypt, and the wider Arab world well into the twentieth century, after printed Arabic Bibles had become widely available, particularly in monasteries and in households that used calligraphic Bibles for liturgical or devotional reading.

The dominant Arabic Bible of the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries was the Smith-Van Dyck Version, completed at Beirut in 1865 under the direction of the Syrian Mission and the American Bible Society. Eli Smith of the American Board began the translation in 1847, and after his death in 1857 Cornelius Van Alen Van Dyck carried it to completion with the Lebanese scholars Butrus al-Bustani and Nasif al-Yaziji. The Van Dyck Bible was printed in Beirut by the American Mission Press, which produced its own Arabic type cut specifically for the project. The version became the standard Arabic Scripture for Protestants across the Ottoman Empire and was eventually adopted by many Orthodox and Catholic readers as well (Griffith 2013). A handwritten Arabic New Testament dated 1908 most likely reproduces the Van Dyck text or a closely related liturgical version used by a specific Arab Christian community.

Manuscripts of this period typically use a careful naskh script, with red ink for chapter and verse headings, occasional illuminated headpieces at the opening of each Gospel, and Arabic numerals for chapter divisions. Melkite, Maronite, Coptic Orthodox, Syriac Catholic, and Chaldean communities each maintained their own scribal traditions, and the specific provenance of this codex can be recovered only by a scholar examining its hand, orthography, paper, binding, and any inscriptions directly.

he Van Dyck Arabic Bible, published in complete form in 1865 with the Gospel of John available in stand-alone printings from 1867 onward, is the most widely circulated modern Arabic Scripture. The translation was undertaken by the American Syrian Mission at Beirut for the American Bible Society beginning in 1847. Eli Smith, an American missionary and Arabist, directed the project until his death in 1857. Cornelius Van Alen Van Dyck, a New Yorker trained in medicine and Oriental languages, completed the work with the Lebanese scholars Butrus al-Bustani, Nasif al-Yaziji, and the Muslim shaikh Yusuf al-Asir, who vetted the Arabic for classical correctness.

The translation used the Hebrew Masoretic Text for the Old Testament and the Textus Receptus Greek for the New Testament, drawing also on the Syriac Peshitta. A purpose-cut Arabic typeface, the "American Arabic" font designed at Leipzig by Homan Hallock under Smith's direction, was cast in Beirut. The font set a new standard for Arabic typography and was used for scholarly and literary printing across the Levant.

The complete Bible appeared in 1865 from the American Mission Press in Beirut. Separate Gospel printings, including the Gospel of John, were issued for evangelistic distribution and school use from the later 1860s onward. The British and Foreign Bible Society took up joint publication with the American Bible Society from 1866, and the Van Dyck text remains the standard Protestant Arabic Bible of the Middle East, North Africa, and the Arabic-speaking diaspora to the present.

Al-Bustani, who helped shape the Van Dyck text, used Smith's workshop as the seed of his Muhit al-Muhit, the first modern Arabic dictionary (1867 to 1870), and his encyclopedia Da'irat al-Ma'arif, landmarks of the Nahda. The Bible typeface cast for the mission served both projects.

his 1992 Genesis portion is a scripture booklet in Egyptian Arabic (ISO 639-3 arz), the colloquial Arabic spoken by roughly 100 million people in Egypt and widely understood across the Arab world through Egyptian cinema, television, and song. Egyptian Arabic (al-`ammiyya al-misriyya) is distinct in phonology, vocabulary, and syntax from Modern Standard Arabic, which is the language of formal writing and of the classical Van Dyck-Bustani Arabic Bible of 1865 used across the Middle East.

Modern Standard Arabic Scripture has long been in circulation through the Smith-Van Dyck translation, the Jesuit Beirut translation of 1876-1880, and the Today's Arabic Version of the 1970s. Vernacular colloquial Scriptures remained comparatively rare, because the prestige of Modern Standard Arabic and the classical register of the Qur'an shape expectations for religious language across the Arab world.

The Bible Society of Egypt issued a series of Egyptian Arabic colloquial Scriptures from the 1990s onward aimed at readers for whom Standard Arabic is a formal second register rather than an everyday medium. The 1992 Genesis portion, carrying the "Standard" label on its cover, uses an accessible Egyptian Arabic register in Arabic script and was intended to make the creation and patriarchal narratives available to a wider readership, including Coptic Orthodox, Coptic Catholic, and Protestant families. The booklet complements the Society's longer-established Modern Standard Arabic Bible distribution and its Cairo-published scripture literature for children and new readers.

orth Levantine Arabic (ISO 639-3 apc) is the spoken vernacular of Syria and Lebanon, with roughly 25 million speakers. It is sharply distinct from Modern Standard Arabic in grammar, vocabulary, and phonology, though it is diglossic with the standard language and is rarely written outside of plays, song lyrics, social media, and specialized Bible Society diglot editions.

Genesis in spoken North Levantine is part of a wider United Bible Societies and partner-agency initiative, active since the early 2000s, to produce Scripture in the colloquial Arabics alongside the long-established Van Dyck (1865) and New Arabic Version translations in the classical register. Colloquial scripture serves two purposes at once: it makes the biblical narrative immediately audible for listeners with limited formal Arabic schooling, and it provides oral-preference readers with a text that matches the Arabic they actually speak at home.

Production followed the common UBS practice for colloquial editions: a translation base in Modern Standard Arabic was adapted by native-speaker consultants into Levantine phrasing, checked against the Hebrew Masoretic Text for narrative accuracy, and circulated in audio alongside print. The printed portion uses the Arabic script with supplementary diacritics to mark Levantine vowel qualities and the shift of the qaf to a glottal stop in urban speech.

his Shuwa Gospel of Luke is a late twentieth-century scripture portion in Chadian Arabic (ISO 639-3 shu), commonly called Shuwa or Baggara Arabic, a variety of spoken Arabic used by about 1.6 million people as a first language and many more as a second language across the Lake Chad basin, from central and southern Chad into northeastern Nigeria (Borno State), northern Cameroon (Far North Region), and southwestern Sudan. The Shuwa Arabs are descendants of Arab migrants who moved west from Sudan into the Lake Chad basin in the thirteenth to nineteenth centuries and retained Arabic while adopting local cattle-herding livelihoods.

Shuwa Arabic is distinct from Modern Standard Arabic and from the Sudanese Arabic of Khartoum, and for many Lake Chad speakers the classical Bible translations in Standard Arabic are difficult to follow. Vernacular scripture work in Shuwa was taken up by SIL and the Bible Societies of Chad and Nigeria from the late twentieth century, producing Gospel portions and narrative translations.

The Gospel of Luke in this edition is printed in a Shuwa Arabic orthography using Arabic script adapted to the dialect's phonology, and was distributed through Catholic missions of the Diocese of N'Djamena and Sarh and through evangelical and SIM (Sudan Interior Mission) congregations in Chad, northeast Nigeria, and northern Cameroon.

he 1992 Tajik Genesis portion is an Institute for Bible Translation (IBT) edition in Tajik (ISO 639-3 tgk), the Eastern Iranian / Persian variety spoken by about eight million people in Tajikistan and in the cities of Samarkand and Bukhara in Uzbekistan. Tajik is mutually intelligible with the Farsi of Iran and the Dari of Afghanistan, but in the Soviet and post-Soviet period has been written in the Cyrillic alphabet with several Tajik-specific letters, a legacy of the 1939 Cyrillisation that replaced the earlier Perso-Arabic Nastaliq and a short-lived Latin alphabet.

The Institute for Bible Translation, founded in Stockholm in 1973 by Borislav Arapović to produce Scripture for the non-Slavic peoples of the Soviet Union, launched Tajik translation in the late 1980s and produced a sequence of Old and New Testament portions through the 1990s. The 1992 Genesis is among the earliest of these, appearing just after Tajikistan's independence in September 1991 and during the run-up to the civil war of 1992-1997.

The volume is a softcover Cyrillic-script portion in the standard Tajik orthography with the distinctive ӣ, ӯ, ҳ, ҷ, ғ, and қ characters. Distribution has been chiefly through the small ethnic Russian and Tajik Protestant communities of Dushanbe, Khujand, and Kulob, and via IBT's international partners abroad.
